title: Anthropic Begins Work on Custom AI Chips to Rival OpenAI
summary:
The AI startup has begun developing its own proprietary silicon to reduce its reliance on external chip designers and lower the cost of its compute infrastructure. The company has set a target to complete its chip program in half the time it took OpenAI to produce its first-generation hardware.

Moving chip design in-house would allow AI labs to bypass margins charged by firms such as Nvidia, Broadcom and Marvell, potentially reducing the cost of building a gigawatt of compute to $20 billion from $60 billion, Dylan Patel of SemiAnalysis said. The move follows tests on the open-source InferenceX benchmark that showed OpenAI's first-generation chip outperformed Nvidia's Blackwell when running Chinese models.

selectedTweets.text:
Dylan Patel says Anthropic aims to build its chip in half the time OpenAI took, and explains how, without chip designers’ margins, a gigawatt costs about $20 billion, not $60 billion

“I mean, that’s certainly the trend, is all of these companies are trying to make chips, right? OpenAI showed, I think for the first time ever in the industry, that you can make a first-generation chip that’s really good. They let us into the lab. We tested on our open-source InferenceX benchmark, running all these open-source Chinese models, and the performance was better than Blackwell. And that’s a first-generation chip, and they utilized AI heavily in the design and programming process."

"And Anthropic is starting their chip program, and they want to do it in half the time that OpenAI did. So they want to get a chip. I mean, these are aggressive goals, but if models are able to help them, you know, really accelerate this process. You’ve got Google selling TPUs externally, you’ve got Amazon’s Trainium, really quite good now and fully usable in PyTorch and such, Meta’s very aggressive roadmap, Microsoft, et cetera."

"If you look at the, you know, I said it went from $40 billion to build a gigawatt to 60. If you remove all the margin out of the chip design houses, right, the NVIDIA and Broadcom, Marvell, et cetera, you’re actually at like $20 billion a gigawatt."

"And so, if you were able to do that, then you could pay for five gigawatts with one gigawatt worth of compute running inference. And so obviously the economics here are very aligned. And as Stacy said, these companies just have to run like crazy, right? You can’t afford to be 2x performance per dollar per year, because you’re going to get completely smashed by these other companies, right?”
